Electro Swing is a musical genre combining the influence of vintage or modern Swing and Jazz mixed with House, Hip Hop and EDM. Electro Swing is the use of Jazz samples from a Jazz record (either classic or modern) swing, jazz and big band era plus modern beats.The period starts from the early 1930s to the late 1940s and would include music by Duke Ellington, Cab Calloway, Lionel Hampton and Benny Goodman among many others. Successful examples of the genre create a modern and dance-floor focused sound that is more readily accessible to the modern ear but that also retains the feeling of live brass and the energetic excitement of the early swing recordings. The best-known artists include Parov Stelar and Caravan Palace while one-off international hits include 'Why Don't You Do Right?' by Gramophonedzie or Nr. 1 World Hit We No Speak Americano by Australian duo Yolanda Be Cool Vs DCUP.

In addition to individual artists and one-off hits, Electro Swing is a genre whose growth has largely been fuelled by a series of European compilation albums which have drawn together works by a variety of producers. These include the British 'White Mink : Black Cotton' series described by Mixmag as "Electro Swing's first landmark moment"[1] and France's 'Electro Swing' series. In the United States, parties such as San Francisco's 'Trapeze' have showcased the genre's artists.

Taken from WIkipedia article on the genre

To the right on every subreddit is a list of moderators for that subreddit. Each moderator should have a checkmark next to it defaulted checked. If unchecked all changes, spam removals, comments, censorship by that mod becomes undone and visible but only for the person unchecking it.

I think this should be extendable to all users. Every user should be able to be able to block/censor another user but only from their own point of view. Like in an MMO when you mute someone.

If implemented on reddit or voat for example, people would no longer be able to complain about shitty mods, if they really think a mod causes more harm than good they can block that user. Sure they would see all the spam they removed, but they would also see all that that person censored.

Before designing a centralized system to overthrow moderators, lets decentralize the decision to the point of view of each user, it will render a lot of the problem moot.

This a really nice idea although I don't see how you can do this for user that's been banned. If somebody spams a subverse and gets banned. Will he still be able to post in that subverse and only users who 'unchecked' the mod will be able to see his content?
I think this is an ideal solution, mods can have user blacklists which by default filter the channel, and users can simply toggle on/off a mod's blacklist at their discretion. Nothing to lose.

It's still really tricky as you can have a mod who bans alternative views and trolls. Nobody wants to have trolls but everyone wants to see the alternative views that has been banned. So you would have to choose.

I think a better solution to this is to have complete moderator accountability. Mod's actions should be transparent and open to public view. Though I agree that local user blocking has good merit to it as well. Thats a feature that can not hurt the community as a whole. In the end though, if Voat is to be the free speech and transparent haven it wants to be, the actions of those who govern should be open to criticism to those they serve.
